expect:
Two marks per point:
• Jesus's final cry — 'My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?' — quotes Psalm 22, a psalm that begins in abandonment but moves toward vindication; this shows him as the suffering servant of the scriptures whose death fulfils God's plan.
• The centurion's confession — 'Surely this man was the Son of God' — is the theological climax of Mark's Gospel; the first human to correctly identify Jesus during his lifetime is a Gentile Roman soldier, showing that the cross reveals Jesus's identity and that salvation is for all peoples.
value:
Two marks per point:
• Jesus's final cry — 'My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?' — quotes Psalm 22, a psalm that begins in abandonment but moves toward vindication; this shows him as the suffering servant of the scriptures whose death fulfils God's plan.
• The centurion's confession — 'Surely this man was the Son of God' — is the theological climax of Mark's Gospel; the first human in Mark to call Jesus the Son of God is a Gentile Roman soldier, speaking just after the death, showing that the cross reveals Jesus's identity and that salvation is for all peoples.
note: F14: the centurion speaks after Jesus has died

expect: The Jewish ruling council, also called the Sanhedrin; led by the High Priest, it had authority over religious law and could recommend the death penalty to the Romans.

note: F13: the entry defined the council, not the person
